title: Fal says the new round is closed. The $16 billion figure is Bloomberg's, via TechCrunch
friendlyTitle: Fal says the new funding round is closed. The $16 billion figure comes from a news report
summary: TechCrunch, citing Bloomberg, reports that Fal raised $1.3 billion in a round led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with Nvidia, Sound Ventures, and T. Rowe Price, at a $16 billion valuation. That is double the $8 billion valuation Bloomberg reported for April. Fal's own post, published the same day, confirms a Series E led by Sequoia and a Series F led by Bessemer, with Nvidia as a strategic investor. It does not state the amounts. TechCrunch says Fal put the two rounds at a combined $1.65 billion. Bloomberg, via TechCrunch, also says Fal passed $800 million in annualized revenue earlier this year. TechCrunch adds that people familiar with inference businesses say gross margins stay thin because compute is expensive.
friendlySummary: TechCrunch, citing Bloomberg, reports that Fal raised $1.3 billion in a round led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with Nvidia, Sound Ventures, and T. Rowe Price. The reported valuation is $16 billion, double the $8 billion Bloomberg reported for April. Fal's own post, published the same day, confirms an earlier round led by Sequoia and a new round led by Bessemer, with Nvidia as a strategic investor. It does not state the amounts. TechCrunch says Fal put the two rounds at a combined $1.65 billion. Bloomberg, via TechCrunch, also says Fal passed $800 million in annualized revenue earlier this year. TechCrunch adds that people familiar with this kind of business say profit margins stay thin because the computers are expensive.
whyItMatters: Fal runs other companies' image, video, and audio models. A higher valuation does not change the price on your invoice. If you depend on a hosted model, the useful question is whether the provider can keep serving it when the margin is thin, not whether the last round was $16 billion. That figure is a report, not a number Fal printed.
